Why Do Irish Domestic Payments Fail?

⚑  Core finding: Ireland's payment failure problem is a data infrastructure problem, not a system capacity problem. The payment system is functioning correctly — it is correctly rejecting payments to wrong, closed, or blocked accounts. The EU Verification of Payee mandate went live in Ireland in October 2025; our 2024 data quantifies what it would have prevented — at least 25% of all failures, with disproportionate financial impact on the B2B corridor.

Key Findings

  • Account Problems cause 60.2% of all failures — AC01 wrong IBAN (25.1%), AC04 closed account (19.9%), AC06 blocked account (15.2%). The payment system is working correctly; the account data is not.
  • EU VoP mandate prevents 25–45% of failures: AC01 directly preventable (10,606 transactions, €1.65M value at risk); upper bound 45% if AC04 partial intercept included. AC06 is NOT addressable by VoP — it requires PSP-level account management.
  • Merchant value inversion: merchants are 9.9% of failures by count but 57.1% by value — VoP delivers 12× more financial protection per B2B event than per consumer event.
  • Data Quality failures dominated by a single fixable field: BE04 (missing creditor address) accounts for 88.5% of all Data Quality failures — a single mandatory field validation at payment initiation would eliminate 4,268 failures immediately.

Data Architecture & Methodology

Datasets Used

DatasetDescriptionIE ScopeRoleJoin Validation
D01 Retail payment transactions (12 monthly tables) 2,125,237 IE rows (corridor LIKE 'Domestic_IE%') Primary source — outcome variable and all transaction characteristics 100% — SQL COUNT confirmed per month
D03 Settlement logs (3,312,099 total rows) 1,406,503 IE rows (IE derived from D01 transaction_ids) ISO 20022 error codes — WHY each failure occurred. event_type and settlement_status are identical columns. 100% on failure records — all 42,269 failures matched to Rejected records. Overall IE coverage: 66.2%.
D10 IE profiles (Consumer + Merchant) 450,000 Consumer + 50,000 Merchant IE profiles Consumer demographics and merchant segment. Loaded separately by profile_type. 100% after dual load — Consumer (90.1% of failures) and Merchant (9.9%) populations joined separately.
D06 IE PSP registry 296 IE PSPs Market structure — institution type, instant readiness 100% — all 296 PSP IDs matched

D03 Coverage — What the Gap Means

D03 covers 66.2% of IE transactions overall (1,406,503 of 2,125,237). However, all 42,269 failures have D03 records — the coverage gap affects only completed transactions and does not impact failure analysis.

100% D03 presence

  • E_Money — all completed transactions logged
  • SEPA_Instant — all instant payments logged
  • is_instant = True — 100% presence

~60% D03 presence

  • Card — 59.95% of completed transactions logged
  • Credit_Transfer — 59.88% logged
  • Direct_Debit — 60.06% logged
D03 likely captures all instant payment processing and ~60% of traditional payment processing. The remaining ~40% of traditional payments appear to settle through a card-network pathway that does not generate a D03 record. This does not affect failure analysis: all 42,269 failures have D03 records regardless of instrument type.

Key Methodology Notes

  • Failure rate normalisation: All hourly and day-type comparisons use failures per 1,000 transactions (not raw counts) to control for volume variation across hours and days
  • No synthetic metrics: Every figure in this report derives directly from a raw database field — no composite scores, no modelled estimates, no weighted indices
  • Merchant population: D10 was loaded twice — Consumer (profile_type='Consumer') and Merchant (profile_type='Merchant') — and failure populations analysed separately. The merchant population was initially missed and required a separate load.

Top Error Codes — Detail & Policy Actions

CodeDescription% of FailuresVoP Addresses This?Policy Action
AC01 Incorrect account number (wrong IBAN) 25.1% YES — directly VoP live in Ireland from October 2025 — Netherlands CoSP saw ~67% reduction in misdirected payments post-implementation.
AC04 Closed account 19.9% PARTIAL Account closure notification registry — UK CASS model redirects payments for 3 years post-closure. No Irish equivalent.
AC06 Blocked account 15.2% NOT addressable PSP-to-PSP account status API needed — no confirmed international precedent at scale. Requires CBI regulatory framework.
AM04 Insufficient funds 12.2% NOT addressable Irreducible under current framework — monitor as SEPA Instant mandate increases irreversibility consequences.
BE04 Missing creditor address 10.1% NOT by VoP Enforce ISO 20022 mandatory field at payment initiation — eliminates 88.5% of all Data Quality failures immediately.
AG01 Transaction forbidden 8.2% NOT addressable System working correctly — mandate block reason transparency to end-users rather than reducing blocks.
MS03 Reason not specified 5.1% — Mandate ISO 20022 code specificity — CBI enforcement of existing ECB guidelines.
F1
60.2% of failures share a single root cause: undeliverable account data

AC01 (wrong IBAN), AC04 (closed account), and AC06 (blocked account) together account for 60.2% of all failures. These are not infrastructure failures — the settlement layer is correctly rejecting payments directed at accounts that cannot receive them. The root problem is stale, incorrect, or unresolvable account data at the payment initiation layer. Investment in payment infrastructure capacity will not reduce these failures; data quality intervention — specifically IBAN-name verification at the point of initiation — will.

AM04 (Insufficient Funds) shows no significant demographic variation across any tested dimension — segment, age band, income band, tenure, or vulnerability flag — with p-values ranging from 0.445 to 0.983. This flat distribution is consistent with synthetic data generation rather than real-world behaviour.

F2
Merchant AC01 failures represent 56% of AC01 value despite 9.9% of count

Merchant AC01 failures: 1,054 transactions, €921,873 total value, €874.64 average per event. Consumer AC01 failures: 9,552 transactions, €723,870 total value, €75.78 average per event. A regulator prioritising VoP should focus on the B2B payment corridor — where each prevented failure saves 12× more value — before considering the wider cash flow disruption B2B payment failures cause for Irish businesses. The Utilities sector stands out with an AC01 rate of 35.9% vs 25.1% overall, suggesting a specific problem with outdated direct debit mandate data warranting targeted investigation.

Testing for error profile differences between consumer and merchant populations: We tested whether error code distributions differed between the two populations. They did not — distributions are near-identical across all categories (max difference: 0.91pp). This uniformity is consistent with synthetic data generation rather than real-world behaviour. In real transaction data, we would expect merchants to show higher AC04 rates (stale supplier account databases) and lower AM04 rates (business working capital buffers). This question cannot be answered from synthetic data and warrants investigation with real CBI transaction records.

When Do Payments Fail?

Hourly Failure Rate by Category

All rates are per 1,000 transactions, controlling for volume variation. Hover over the chart to see rates by category and hour.

Failure Rate by Hour of Day (per 1,000 transactions)
Account Problem failures average ~12 per 1,000 transactions across all hours — a structural data quality issue, not a time-of-day phenomenon.
F3
Weekend Account Problem rate marginally higher — directional observation only

After controlling for transaction volume, Account Problem failures show a weekend rate of 20.29 per 1,000 transactions versus 19.80 on weekdays (+2.46% relative uplift). The direction is consistent with automated payments running on weekends against stale or closed accounts. However, statistical evidence is mixed:

TestWhat it assumesResultConclusion
Independent samples t-testDaily rates normally distributedt=2.24, p=0.026Significant at α=0.05
Mann-Whitney U testNo distributional assumption (more robust)U=15,237, p=0.077Not significant at α=0.05
Cohen's d (effect size)—d=0.25Small effect — practically minor

We present this as a directional observation worth monitoring, not a strong finding.

Weekday vs Weekend Failure Rate by Category (per 1,000 transactions)
Note: directional observation only — see statistical qualification in Finding F3 above.
F4
Data Quality and Authorisation failures fall sharply on weekends

Data Quality failures are -43.9% and Authorisation failures are -43.5% on weekends compared to weekday daily averages. Both failure types are associated with active business payment initiation — corporate B2B payments and batch compliance processing — which concentrates in weekday business hours. AG01 authorisation failures reach their daily maximum at 04:00 (2.03 per 1,000 transactions versus a minimum of 1.26 at 05:00) — modest variation consistent with overnight automated compliance screening runs, not a dramatic spike.

6
Data Quality & Authorisation Deep Dive

Beyond the top-line error taxonomy, we conducted deeper analysis on two categories where the data revealed specific actionable patterns: Data Quality (11.4% of failures, where a single root cause dominates) and Authorisation (8.3% of failures, where timing patterns are visible). Account Problems and Liquidity failures are covered in Sections 3 and 4.

The PSP type and consumer segment breakdowns show near-identical error code distributions across all groups. This is a synthetic data artefact — no conclusions about institutional or demographic differences in failure profiles can be drawn from these cross-tabs.
Charts ⑥ & ⑦ — Error category mix by PSP type and consumer segment (stacked bars, each summing to 100%). Distributions are near-identical across all groups — consistent with synthetic data generation. No cross-dimensional conclusions are valid from these cross-tabs.

Data Quality Failures — Almost Entirely One Fixable Field

BE04 accounts for 10.1% of all 42,269 failures (88.5% of the Data Quality category). A single mandatory field fix at payment initiation eliminates the vast majority of an entire failure category at zero infrastructure cost.
Error CodeDescription% of DQ FailuresFix Required
BE04Missing creditor address88.5%Single mandatory field at payment initiation
DT01Invalid date1.1%Date format validation
RF01Non-unique transaction reference1.1%Duplicate reference check at submission
MD02Missing mandatory information1.1%Mandatory field checklist
RR02Missing debtor name/address1.1%Mandatory field at initiation
Other DQ codesVarious (BE05, DT02, DT04, RR01, RR03, RR04, BE07, BE06)7.0%Structured field validation

Authorisation Patterns

  • AG01 (Transaction Forbidden) = 8.2% of all failures — deliberate compliance/sanctions blocks; the system is functioning correctly
  • AG01 reaches its daily maximum at 04:00 (2.03 per 1,000 transactions, minimum 1.26 at 05:00) — modest variation consistent with overnight batch compliance screening
  • Authorisation failures drop -43.5% on weekends vs weekday averages — reflecting weekday concentration of corporate batch payment initiation
  • Policy focus should be on transparency of block reasons to end-users, not reduction of blocks

Cost & Financial Impact

Total transaction value at risk across all 42,269 IE domestic failures: €6,570,087.

€6,570,087
Total transaction value at risk (confirmed from D01 amount field)
€372.96
Total D03 processing cost — €0.0088 avg per failure (settlement infrastructure fee only)
63,679
Total retries generated by 42,269 failures (avg 1.51 per failure, D03 retry_count)
+161ms
Extra processing time per rejected transaction vs settled (1,789ms vs 1,628ms median, p<0.001)
The €372.96 total processing cost captures only the settlement infrastructure fee — €0.0088 per failed transaction. This is negligible. The real financial impact is the €6,570,087 of transaction value that did not reach its intended destination — money that was not paid to suppliers, landlords, employees, or service providers. The downstream consequences (late payment penalties, missed service access, merchant cash flow disruption, consumer distress) are not captured in any of the four datasets and represent the true cost of payment failure to the Irish economy.

Retry Pattern

Retry counts are uniformly distributed across 0–3 retries (~25% each) — a synthetic data artefact. In real-world data, AM04 failures would show higher retry rates as payers replenish funds, and AG01 failures would show lower rates as blocks are typically definitive. No valid retry pattern conclusions can be drawn from this data.

8
Policy Recommendations
PriorityRecommendationEvidenceInternational PrecedentExpected Impact
CRITICAL Monitor and evaluate EU Verification of Payee implementation — prioritise B2B corridor AC01 = 25.1% of failures. Merchant AC01 = 56% of AC01 value despite 9.9% of count. VoP delivers 12× more per B2B event. Our 2024 data predates implementation and quantifies what VoP would have prevented. VoP live in Ireland from October 2025 (EU Instant Payments Regulation). Netherlands CoSP saw ~67% reduction. UK CoP live since 2020. Prevent 10,606–19,020 failures. €1.65M+ value protected. Largest benefit in B2B/merchant corridor.
CRITICAL Mandate creditor address (BE04) as required field at payment initiation BE04 = 10.1% of all failures (88.5% of the Data Quality category). Single mandatory field, zero infrastructure cost. ISO 20022 full data requirements already specify this — enforcement is the gap, not legislation. ECB SEPA guidance mandates BE04 compliance. Eliminate up to 4,268 failures. Achievable immediately via PSP-level form validation.
HIGH Introduce account closure notification registry (AC04 — closed accounts) AC04 = 19.9% of all failures. IBAN exists but account is closed — VoP alone will not catch these. UK's Current Account Switch Service (CASS) automatically redirects and notifies for 3 years post-closure. No Irish equivalent. Significant reduction in AC04 failures over time. Requires inter-PSP cooperation and CBI coordination.
HIGH Standardise PSP-to-PSP account status API (AC06 — blocked accounts) AC06 = 15.2% of failures. NOT addressable by VoP. Account exists and IBAN is correct but is blocked. No confirmed international precedent at scale. PSD2 open banking APIs could be extended — requires CBI regulatory framework for account status data sharing. Reduce 6,425 AC06 failures. Requires new regulatory framework.
MEDIUM Investigate Utilities sector AC01 spike Utilities AC01 rate = 35.9% vs 25.1% average — 10.8pp above average. Confirmed from D01+D10 merchant data. Suggests systematic stale account data in direct debit mandates. Targeted mandate refresh campaigns — similar to UK CRU (Commission for Regulation of Utilities) periodic mandate audits. Disproportionate reduction in Utilities AC01 failures. Low cost, targeted intervention.
MEDIUM Monitor AM04 (insufficient funds) as SEPA Instant mandate expands 12.2% of failures are AM04. Under instant payment irreversibility, each AM04 failure is definitive — payer must initiate a new payment. SEPA Instant mandate increases AM04 consequences. Pre-payment balance check frameworks under PSD2 open banking require payer consent. Quantify consumer welfare cost as SEPA Instant adoption grows.
LOW Mandate ISO 20022 error code specificity — eliminate MS03 "unspecified" MS03 (reason not specified) = 5.1% of failures. Absence of specific code obscures root cause analysis. ECB SEPA guidelines already require specific codes. CBI enforcement action against PSPs using MS03 without justification. Improves failure root cause visibility. No direct failure reduction but improves regulatory oversight.
9
Limitations & Caveats
LimitationImpactWhat It Affects
Synthetic data uniformity High Error distributions are uniform across all segments and instruments — cross-dimensional comparisons are invalid. Value findings (€74 consumer vs €898 merchant) are real and data-evidenced; error profile similarity is a synthetic artefact.
D03 coverage: 66.2% of IE transactions Medium All 42,269 failures have D03 records. The 33.8% gap affects completed transactions only — settlement pathway conclusions for non-failure payments are incomplete.
VoP impact is a range, not a precise figure Medium AC01 count (25.1%) is observed directly. Actual VoP intercept rate depends on implementation. Range: 25.1% conservative to 45% upper bound.
Weekend finding: mixed statistical significance Medium t-test p=0.026 significant; Mann-Whitney U p=0.077 not significant; Cohen's d=0.25 (small). Presented as directional observation only.
D03 cost captures infrastructure fees only Medium €372.96 total understates true cost — operational, friction, and cash flow costs are absent from all four datasets.
Retry counts synthetically uniform Low 0–3 retries at ~25% each regardless of error type. No real retry pattern conclusions valid. Real AM04 would retry more; AG01 less.
No benchmark against CBI published statistics Low CBI published datasets are value-based, not failure-rate-based. The 1.989% failure rate cannot be validated against published figures.
